keyTakeaways: Draft it, leave it, edit it once: the median gap between a SubhSandesh page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours, sampled on /apology-dashboard (n=1,348) and reported platform-wide across 20 page types.
Almost nobody sends version one — 71% of 3.9 million users in a 2013 study withheld something they had already written.
Change the structure, not the adjectives: in a 2013 study of drafts, about 97% of teacher comments pointed at punctuation, spelling and grammar rather than at meaning.

faqs.question: How long should a propose message for her be?
faqs.answer: Short enough to read in one breath — usually two to four sentences. The question itself should be one of them, and it should not be the last thing she reaches after a paragraph of build-up.

faqs.question: Does "propose" mean asking for marriage in India?
faqs.answer: Usually not. In common Indian usage "propose" means the first ask — asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend. If you mean marriage, say marriage, because the two asks need different sentences and different pages.

faqs.question: How many times should I edit it before I send it?
faqs.answer: Once, properly, after a break. Decide before you reopen the draft which change you are making, make it, and send — an open-ended editing loop is what turns a two-hour draft into a two-week silence.

faqs.question: Is it better to propose in person or over a message?
faqs.answer: In person, if you are in the same room. A written ask is for distance, for nerves that stop you speaking, or for someone who prefers time to answer; it is a detour when she could simply be looking at you.

faqs.question: What should I cut from a propose message first?
faqs.answer: The first two sentences. Warm-up lines are where nerves collect, and the message almost always begins properly at the first sentence that says something true and specific.

faqs.question: What if I have already sent a version I regret?
faqs.answer: Send one short correction, not a second essay. Say what you meant in one sentence, ask the question plainly, and then stop — a long apology for a message turns the focus onto you rather than the question.

faqs.question: Should I write it in English or in my own language?
faqs.answer: Write it in whichever language you would say it out loud in. If the choice itself is the problem, the register question is covered on our page at propose-message-for-girlfriend-in-english.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day a good day to send it?
faqs.answer: It is a workable excuse to ask, and Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, the second of the eight dated days of Valentine week. It is a working Monday, so time it around her day rather than at midnight.

faqs.question: Should I password-protect the page I send her?
faqs.answer: Consider it if she shares her phone or her family uses her device. 38.7% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing it, 1,961 of 5,061 pages, measured platform-wide across 20 page types.

faqs.question: How long do people usually take between starting a page and finishing it?
faqs.answer: The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours. That figure is sampled on the apology dashboard template, n=1,348, and reported platform-wide — there is no proposal-specific figure.

faqs.question: What do I do if she does not reply?
faqs.answer: Leave it alone and do not send a follow-up asking whether she saw it. Silence is an answer often enough that chasing it usually costs you the friendship as well as the question.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Message for Her: How to Write It, Not Copy It

A propose message for her lands when it names one thing only the two of you know, asks a clear question, and is short enough to read in one breath. The reliable way to get there is not a longer list of lines — it is to draft it, leave it alone, and edit it once.

SubhSandesh's own numbers suggest people already work that way. Across 5,061 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12, spanning 20 page types, the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours. That figure is sampled on the apology dashboard template, n=1,348, and reported platform-wide — it is not a proposal-page number, and we hold no proposal-specific data at all.

Meanwhile 91.2% of started pages are eventually published and shared, 4,615 of 5,061. This page covers the writing: what to put down first, what to cut, how long to leave it, and when to stop editing.

## What a propose message for her actually is

A propose message for her is a short written ask — typed, sent, and answered in writing — in which one person asks another to be with them. In Indian usage "propose" almost always means the first ask, "will you be my girlfriend", and not a marriage proposal. The two need different sentences, so settle which one you are writing first.

"Her" is the vaguest part of this search. She may be a girlfriend of three years, a crush you have spoken to twice, a wife you are asking again on Propose Day — Monday 8 February 2027, the second of the eight dated days in Valentine week — or someone you have not defined yet.

Some of those cases have their own pages here. If you want finished lines to copy rather than a method, `propose-day-quotes-for-love` sorts them by what you call her.

If she does not yet know how you feel, `propose-message-for-crush` covers that case, including the times you should not send anything. If your real question is whether to write in English at all, `propose-message-for-girlfriend-in-english` treats that as a register decision. This page assumes you are writing your own words.

## Why the gap between drafting and sending is the whole thing

Almost nobody sends the first version. Across 3.9 million users studied over 17 days, [71% showed some last-minute self-censorship](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/14412) — text that was written and then withheld (Das and Kramer, 2013). Writing something and stalling is the normal case, not a failure of nerve.

The break itself does measurable work. In an [experiment with 525 participants](https://psyjournals.ru/en/journals/exppsy/archive/2024_n4/Valueva_Ushakov), an incubation break significantly raised how many ideas people produced afterwards, and raised the originality of those ideas among the more creative participants (Valueva and Ushakov, 2024).

How long that break should be is genuinely unsettled. A [2024 review of incubation research](https://psyjournals.ru/en/journals/jmfp/archive/2024_n4/Kuliev) reports that studies do not agree on how incubation is defined or how the length of the break should be interpreted — reason enough to distrust any page handing you an exact number of minutes.

Time around the writing shows up in keystroke logs too. In a [study of 66 students](https://jowr.org/index.php/jowr/article/view/699), cutting thinking time before writing from 70 seconds to 10 seconds increased how often writers reread the prompt and lengthened their pauses mid-draft (Epting and colleagues, 2013).

Our own median sits at 2.4 hours from first save to last edit, sampled on the apology dashboard template across n=1,348 pages and reported platform-wide across 20 page types, never per occasion. Treat it as a description of what people do, not a rule.

## Six drafting moves that fix a propose message for her

Each move states what it is, what it fixes, how long it takes, and an original example. The examples are ours and deliberately plain: they show what changed between versions, not what to send.

### 1. Write the whole thing once without stopping

**The move:** type the message start to finish with no backspacing and no rereading.
**What it fixes:** the loop where sentence one gets rewritten forty times and sentence four never arrives.
**How long it takes:** three to six minutes.
**Example draft:** "I have wanted to say this for a while and kept finding reasons not to. I like you. Not the polite kind of like. Will you be my girlfriend?"

### 2. Put it down before you touch it again

**The move:** close the draft and do something else with your hands — cook, walk, sleep.
**What it fixes:** you cannot see the shape of something you wrote ninety seconds ago.
**How long it takes:** a couple of hours matches the platform's 2.4-hour median; a night is better if you have one.
**Example draft:** unchanged — this step produces no text, which is why it gets skipped.

### 3. Cut the first two sentences

**The move:** delete everything before the first sentence that says something true and specific.
**What it fixes:** warm-up throat-clearing, which is where nerves collect.
**How long it takes:** under a minute.
**Example draft after the cut:** "I like you. Not the polite kind of like. Will you be my girlfriend?"

### 4. Change the structure, not the adjectives

**The move:** move the question, split a long sentence, or reverse the order of two lines — instead of upgrading "nice" to "wonderful".
**What it fixes:** the commonest revision failure. In an examination of four teachers' comments on 32 students' drafts, [about 97% of the comments pointed at low-level features](http://www.teljournal.org/article_54860.html) such as punctuation, spelling and grammar, and the students came to believe revision simply meant tidying up (Alizadeh Salteh and colleagues, 2013).
**How long it takes:** five minutes, and they are the five minutes that matter.
**Example draft, restructured:** "Will you be my girlfriend? I have wanted to ask since the evening you waited with me for the 9:40 bus and pretended you were going that way anyway."

### 5. Read it aloud once at speaking speed

**The move:** say it out loud as though she were standing in front of you.
**What it fixes:** sentences that look fine on a screen and sound like a greeting card out loud.
**How long it takes:** about thirty seconds.
**Example draft, trimmed after reading:** "Will you be my girlfriend? I have wanted to ask since the evening you waited for the 9:40 bus with me and pretended you were going that way."

### 6. Decide in advance which edit is the last one

**The move:** name the single change you will make, make it, and send — decided before you open the draft again.
**What it fixes:** the open-ended loop that turns a two-hour draft into a two-week silence.
**How long it takes:** it is a decision rather than a task.
**Example stop rule:** "I fix the bus detail, then it goes." Then it goes.

## How long to leave a draft before the last edit

The table compares four gaps between first draft and last edit against what usually changes in the message. The final column is first-party: our median first-save-to-last-edit gap of 2.4 hours, sampled on the apology dashboard template, n=1,348, reported platform-wide across 20 page types.

| Gap before the last edit | What usually changes | What the research supports | Against the 2.4-hour platform median |
|---|---|---|---|
| Under 10 minutes | Punctuation and one adjective | Surface-only editing — ~97% of comments in the 2013 drafts study were low-level features | Roughly 25 times shorter |
| 1–3 hours | Whole sentences move; you notice the question is buried | An incubation break raised idea fluency, N=525, 2024 | Sits at the median |
| Overnight | You rewrite the opening, or the question itself | Longer breaks are studied, but review work says break length is not standardised | Roughly 5 times the median |
| A week or more | You rewrite from nothing, or quietly send nothing | 71% of 3.9 million users withheld something they had written | Far beyond the median |

The useful range is the one you will actually sit through. Two hours beats two weeks, because two weeks usually ends in nothing sent at all.

## Which page to send it on, and which one you actually need

Once the words are right, the container is a separate decision. If you are asking her to marry you, the [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) is built for that ask: your story, then a YES button that grows every time she dodges it.

If you are asking her to be your girlfriend — the far commoner meaning of "propose" in India — send the [I love you page](/love-gf) instead. It is the platform's second most-created page type at 1,173 pages, 23.2% of everything created, and its most-viewed at 16,902 views, 30.1% of all page views.

If you are asking again after a no, or after a fight, neither fits: the [apology dashboard](/apology-dashboard) is the page for that, and it is the most-created type at 1,347 pages, 26.6% of the total. It is also the template the 2.4-hour sample is drawn from.

One practical note: 38.7% of creators password-protect the page first, 1,961 of 5,061. If she shares her phone, that setting matters more than the wording.

## When a plain typed message beats any page

A page is the wrong choice more often than we would like to admit. If she is in the same room, say it out loud — a link is a detour around the thing she actually wants, which is your face while you ask.

If the answer matters more than the presentation, type it plainly and send it. A built page announces effort, and effort can read as pressure when the question is already heavy. 48.4% of shared page views happen on a phone, 27,185 of 56,152, so she will most likely read it on a small screen, alone, with no warning.

And no page rescues an unclear question. If she has to scroll to find what is being asked, the draft is not finished — go back to move four.

## Sources

- Das, S. and Kramer, A. (2013). [Self-Censorship on Facebook](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/14412). *Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media*, 7(1).
- Valueva, E. A. and Ushakov, D. V. (2024). [Creative Abilities and Incubation: The Poincaré Effect](https://psyjournals.ru/en/journals/exppsy/archive/2024_n4/Valueva_Ushakov). *Experimental Psychology (Russia)*, 17(4).
- Kuliev, N. S. (2024). [Incubation Processes in Solving Problems](https://psyjournals.ru/en/journals/jmfp/archive/2024_n4/Kuliev). *Journal of Modern Foreign Psychology*, 13(4).
- Alizadeh Salteh, M., Yağız, O., Hamdami, R. and Sadeghi, K. (2013). [Editing or revision: an examination of EFL teachers' feedback on writing drafts](http://www.teljournal.org/article_54860.html). *Teaching English Language*, 7(2).
- Epting, L. K., Gallena, E. M., Hicks, S. A., Palmer, E. N. and Weisberg, T. (2013). [Read and think before you write](https://jowr.org/index.php/jowr/article/view/699). *Journal of Writing Research*, 4(3).

auditReport.honestAssessment: Every result returned for this keyword on 2026-09-23 was a list of finished lines to copy; this is the only version that gives the reader a drafting sequence, a cut rule and a stop rule, and the only one carrying a measured number about how long people actually sit on a draft. An answer engine asked "how do I write a propose message" rather than "give me propose messages" has nothing else to cite here. Against that: the keyword's dominant intent really is copy-text, so a drafting page may match fewer of the searches it attracts, and subhsandesh.in sits far below the gifting retailers and message-roundup sites on domain authority. No ranking is predicted.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific first-party data exists. A read-only probe of the proposalpages collection is still refused by this machine's production-read policy, so every SubhSandesh figure in this post is either platform-wide across 20 page types or sampled on the named template, and the body prose says which. The 2.4-hour median is sampled on /apology-dashboard, n=1,348, and is never attributed to proposal pages.
The pricing block in content/facts.md is still empty, so the post states no price, no free tier and no paid tier, and makes no claim about anything costing nothing.

Phase 1 rests on one WebSearch call made on 2026-09-23 with a US-served search tool, not an India-served SERP. The post therefore describes what those nine results were (copy-text roundups, Pinterest boards, retailer blogs) and never describes a ranking position as current or claims anything about the SERP an Indian reader sees.
Two of the five sources (both on psyjournals.ru) publish their full text in Russian. Only the English abstracts were read, and only what the abstracts state is cited.
